articles.title: Projetos integrados reúnem automação, conforto e novas tecnologias | G1
articles.standfirst: Breta Instalações amplia atuação em sistemas elétricos, hidráulicos, climatização e automação para residências, comércios e indústrias
articles.summary: Breta Instalações amplia atuação em sistemas elétricos, hidráulicos, climatização e automação para residências, comércios e indústrias
articles.body:
A experiência acumulada ao longo de mais de duas décadas no setor de elétrica e eletrônica foi o ponto de partida para a criação da Breta Instalações. À frente da empresa está Christiano Breta, profissional com formação técnica em Eletrônica e Instrumentação e cursos nas áreas de Engenharia de Produção e Administração.

A trajetória, no entanto, não foi construída apenas dentro da sala de aula. Foi na prática, acompanhando projetos, equipamentos e as transformações tecnológicas do setor, que Christiano desenvolveu a experiência que posteriormente seria incorporada ao próprio negócio.

Em 2019, esse percurso profissional ganhou um novo capítulo. Ao lado da esposa e dos filhos, ele criou a Breta Instalações, inicialmente voltada ao desenvolvimento e à execução de projetos residenciais relacionados a lazer, conforto e bem-estar.

Desde então, a empresa passou por um processo gradual de expansão. O que começou como uma iniciativa familiar passou a envolver também projetos para empresas, comércios e indústrias, ampliando o campo de atuação e a variedade de serviços oferecidos.

Soluções em projetos integrados — Foto: Divulgação/ Breta Instalações.

A evolução dos projetos residenciais, especialmente aqueles voltados ao lazer e ao conforto, também transformou o perfil dos serviços realizados pela empresa.

Piscinas aquecidas com borda infinita, spas em alvenaria, saunas secas e a vapor e sistemas de automação estão entre as especialidades desenvolvidas pela Breta Instalações.

Esses projetos, porém, envolvem uma estrutura que vai muito além do equipamento que aparece no resultado final. Sistemas hidráulicos, elétricos, de aquecimento, climatização e automação precisam funcionar de maneira integrada com um ecossistema prático e funcional.

É nesse contexto que a empresa também atua com sistemas com central de distribuição hidráulica multicamadas de água quente e água fria, sistemas de aquecimento solar, elétrico e a gás, sistema de pressurização inverter e em cascata, rede e central de gás, instalações elétricas e ar-condicionado. A atuação inclui ainda a venda, instalação e manutenção de equipamentos, além de serviços de assistência técnica para marcas do segmento com as quais a empresa trabalha.

Capacitação acompanha avanço tecnológico

A expansão do mercado de equipamentos e sistemas inteligentes trouxe outra necessidade para empresas do setor: a atualização constante.

Na Breta Instalações, a capacitação passou a fazer parte da rotina. Ao longo dos anos, Christiano e sua equipe participaram de treinamentos, cursos e especializações voltados às tecnologias e aos equipamentos utilizados nos projetos. A estratégia acompanha uma mudança percebida no próprio mercado. Com a chegada de sistemas de automação, novas alternativas de aquecimento e equipamentos mais sofisticados, a instalação passou a exigir conhecimento específico sobre diferentes tecnologias e, principalmente, sobre a integração entre elas.

articles.standfirst: Presidente dos EUA elogiou o novo site do governo após fazer comentário sobre sua atuação na Casa Branca
articles.summary: Presidente dos EUA elogiou o novo site do governo após fazer comentário sobre sua atuação na Casa Branca
articles.body:
O presidente dos Estados Unidos , Donald Trump , afirmou nesta terça-feira (29) que teria feito um “trabalho de merda” como presidente caso o lançamento do site America.gov fosse a maior realização de seu governo . Na sequência, porém, elogiou a plataforma.

“Se isso for a maior coisa que já fiz, então fiz um trabalho de merda como presidente. Mas quer saber? Ficou bom pra cacete”, disse Trump durante o evento de lançamento do site, em Washington.

A fala ocorreu durante a apresentação do America.gov, uma plataforma com inteligência artificial voltada para unificar portais do governo e responder dúvidas dos cidadãos com base em informações de fontes oficiais.

Segundo o republicano, quando assessores lhe disseram que o projeto seria o maior feito de sua gestão, Trump teria respondido que, se isso fosse verdade, que ele teria tido um desempenho ruim a frente da Casa Branca.

O site permite, por exemplo, buscar informações sobre serviços como solicitação de passaporte, substituição do cartão do Seguro Social e reservas em parques nacionais. A proposta é reunir em um único endereço serviços que atualmente estão distribuídos por diferentes sites de órgãos federais.

articles.title: 22 homes on Minneapolis’ historic Nicollet Island were put on the market without residents wanting to sell; artists, healers and social workers have now formed a cooperative to try to buy all six Victorian houses together
articles.summary: Families on Nicollet Island have called the houses they have been living in homes for years.
articles.body: Families on Nicollet Island have called the houses they have been living in homes for years. While some work as artists, others as healers and social workers. But recently, they got to know that their homes may have been listed for sale by property managers Twin Cities Housing Development Corporation, a nonprofit based in St. Paul, back in April 2026.Residents have received a letter from the property manager reading that it was "beginning to explore the potential sale of the Nicollet Island Historic Homes buildings." TCHDC manages six historic Victorian houses on Nicollet Island. Divided into a mix of duplexes and fourplexes, there are 22 rental units total, five of which are for low-income households. The affordable housing units are for people earning 50% or less than the area median income, which was nearly $52,000 for two people in Hennepin County in 2025, according to state reports.All six houses were publicly listed on the market on September 10, 2026. Unable to buy their homes back individually, the community of artists, healers and social workers have banded together, attempting to collectively purchase the properties. They legally formed the Nicollet Island Cooperative in August and have since gained the support of neighbours and the East Bank Neighbourhood Partnership.“We have to do our work and do that well, but we also have to be smart enough to figure out how to navigate the system so that we can survive financially,” Patrick Scully, a resident said. In a cooperative, residents collectively own property, democratically elect internal governance and pay monthly operational costs.Executive Director Amanda Novak said TCHDC is operating under a constrained resource environment and dubbed it the reason for its sale. “The decision is a strategic one based on TCHDC’s affordable housing mission and how we can best steward our limited capital, staff capacity and long-term ownership portfolio,” she said. The fourplex in which Scully lives was listed for $670,000 with the others being listed between $450,000 and $750,000. TCHDC is asking $3.94 million for the entire portfolio of six houses.Scully and other residents said they felt disconnected from the higher-income management in their time on the island. Scully said the management has mowed their wildflowers, put salt on their wooden porch despite requests not to and poorly communicated with residents. “What capacity do [property managers] have to really understand what it’s like to be 72 years old, faced with the possibility of having to find a new place to live and figure out if I have to find a new place to live?” Scully asked. “Am I still going to be able to withdraw from my retirement account to support myself, or will I have to take some of that money to pay for where I live? And if I have to do that, maybe I don’t really get to retire. Maybe I just have to keep working.”Novak said coordination with the Minneapolis Heritage Preservation Commission and their third-party management company, MetroPlains, can lengthen service delivery times, and TCHDC takes its responsibilities to residents and historic properties seriously.“We recognise that residents may have concerns about individual maintenance experiences, and we remain committed to meeting our responsibilities to residents and to the City throughout this transition,” Novak said. The cooperative is working with Land Bank Twin Cities, a real-estate investor, to negotiate a deal with TCHDC for purchasing the houses.Nicollet Island Cooperative President Terry Tauger, who has lived on Nicollet Island for more than a year, said the cooperative would protect affordable housing. “It’s more about the people,” Tauger said. “Not just about the houses.”Though no deal has been made, LBTC hopes to purchase the houses from TCHDC on behalf of the cooperative. The cooperative would then enter a repurchasing agreement with the bank, buying the properties over time while allowing tenants to remain. Tauger said this agreement would overcome the hurdle of providing the money upfront and allow the cooperative to organise.Garrett Peterson, program manager at LBTC, said the repurchasing agreement would begin the same day the bank purchases the properties, and would take an estimated one to three years for the cooperative to finish paying.Novak said TCHDC is exploring all options, as long as they show financial stability and will protect the historic properties. “We are open to seriously considering any proposal the Nicollet Island Cooperative submits, just as we would consider other serious proposals for the properties,” Novak said.But nothing is certain until a deal is made. As is the case for Nicollet Island, many of the houses in the area were built in the late 1800s by wealthy families. John Chaffee, who’s lived on Nicollet Island for over five decades, said his home was built in 1873 by a Civil War veteran named George Brookins.The land is owned by the Minneapolis Parks and Recreation Board, but has been leased to the Minneapolis Community Planning and Economic Development department since 1985.CPED leases the properties to Nicollet Island Historic Homes, a limited partnership, of which TCHDC is the managing partner. The limited partnership previously included an investment firm from Boston and a cooperative of residents called Mid-River Neighbourhood Restoration, Inc. The Boston firm exited the limited partnership when federal tax credits ran out, and Mid-River attempted to purchase the properties from TCHDC in 2007 and 2008, but the Great Recession prevented its success.TCHDC had leased the properties to Mid-River since 1988, but announced its switch to individual leases to residents when the second of two leases expired in 2013. The cooperative soon dissolved, and the arrangement has continued since.In an effort to finish what Mid-River started nearly 20 years ago, Nicollet Island Cooperative is working to keep residents in their homes. Kortan said that though some things are out of his control, he is holding onto hope.“Well, I guess if we have to move, hopefully we have a tree out the window,” he said.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: What are BORGs? The college drinking trend taking over TikTok
articles.summary: Proponents argued BORGs made drinking safer. A new study finds otherwise.
articles.body:
Students decorate these alcohol-filled jugs with names like "BORG to be wild" and "Teach me how to Borgie."

A BORG, short for "blackout rage gallon," typically consists of a 1-gallon plastic water jug filled with a mixture of hard alcohol, water and flavor enhancement. It's a drinking trend that has taken TikTok and colleges by storm in recent years, with controversial claims BORGs help reduce drink contamination and hangovers. But a new study, the first to examine BORG use and its consequences among college students, offers a look at the trend's dangers.

Nearly one-third of BORG drinkers report blacking out, according to a study in the Journal of Studies on Alcohol and Drugs , published by Rutgers University. Another 59% report embarrassing behavior and 17% reporting vomiting.

"The thought is, 'great, you control your own beverage, risk contamination, especially in a post-pandemic world, and nobody could alter your beverage,'" says lead researcher Andrea C. King, professor of psychiatry and behavioral neuroscience at the University of Chicago. "That's not really what it is."

The drinks, which are typically DIYed at home, can contain up to a fifth of liquor, or about 17 standard drinks, according to the study, which polled more than 100 participants from a range of private and public U.S. colleges and universities.

That amount of alcohol should be consumed over a week of time, if not longer, says Dr. George Koob, director of the National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism at the National Institutes of Health.

"I wouldn't recommend drinking that amount of alcohol under any circumstances in the context of a party," Koob says.

The drinks often reference popular internet phrases, pop culture moments or memes. A recent TikTok shows a pink, sparkling "Dolly Parton memorial BORG." Others have names like "The GettysBORG Address" and "Hate being SoBORG." The hashtag #borg has more than 31,200 posts on TikTok.

"Fill my BORG with me!" one TikToker announces at the start of a video of her filling a jug with neon-green liquid ahead of St. Patrick's Day. Other videos on the platform show dozens of half-consumed confiscated BORGS lining St. Patrick's Day celebrations and popular college block parties like Boston's Marathon Monday and the University of Wisconsin-Madison's Mifflin party.

Seventy-six percent of BORG drinkers say the beverage helped facilitate conversation, and 62% say it led to more fun than a regular party.

"I'll admit it, how fun that you get to do a clever statement that reflects who you are," King says. "We have a population now that may socially not quite understand how to interact with each other the way maybe prior generations did because there is this online presence, and it may be a great … conversation starter."

One of the earliest social media references to BORGs stems from a March 2020 TikTok . Social media has helped propel the popularity of these drinks on college campuses in the years since, according to King. Google search interest in "BORG" more than tripled in early 2023 and again during the summer of 2025.

In March of 2023, the Amherst fire department dispatched 28 ambulances in response to intoxicated drinking linked to BORGs at University of Massachusetts Amherst parties. Schools including West Virginia University, Northwestern University , the University of Michigan , Stanford University and Boston University have put out notices about the trend on their campus.

When the drinks exploded in popularity in 2023, they drew mixed reactions from experts and internet commentators , with some pointing out that the BORG could reduce drink contamination and spread of sharing-based illness.

"We were drinking gin buckets and jungle juice out of plastic containers and trash cans in the basement of frat houses," millennial content creator Erin Monroe, who is credentialed in substance use prevention in New York, posted in a TikTok about BORGS that garnered more than 1 million likes. "Whether or not they realize they are doing it, this is actually really solid harm reduction … they're deciding what they're drinking, they're keeping it in a closed container and they're bringing it with them everywhere."

But King says this isn't the case. The study found that 95% of participants share their BORGs with others, and King says any of the drink's effects to minimize hangovers would be minimal. Plus, the combination of hard liquor with sweet flavoring from electrolytes, energy drinks or juice may make it easier for someone to consume a large amount of alcohol without realizing it.

What to know about safe alcohol consumption

Young adults' executive functioning, abstract thinking and decision-making skills continue to develop through age 25, and the prefrontal cortex can be impacted by underage drinking, according to Koob.

"The frontal cortex is basically, I always say, it's your super ego," Koob says. "When your frontal cortex isn't working well, and this is a hallmark of intoxication, you're more likely to make rash decisions and impulsive-like activity actions."

Four drinks for a woman and five drinks for a man, consumed over the span of about two hours, typically meets the criteria for binge drinking, according to the National Institutes on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism.

Koob and King recommend having nonalcoholic beverages, like water and soda, on hand at college events as a safe form of hydration. For those of legal drinking age, limit yourself to one standard drink per hour, and alternate every alcohol beverage with a water or seltzer.

"Parents being aware is important," King says. "Most people are finding out about these (BORGs) before they even go to college … on social media, and if the parents don't understand that, then they can't have that conversation."

articles.title: Magic Mountain closes X2 coaster permanently after history of injuries
articles.summary: The X2 ride was for years the Valencia park's crown jewel, the first roller coaster in the world that spun riders 360 degrees in their seats.
articles.body:
Six Flags Magic Mountain's famous X2 roller-coaster ride is permanently closed, following a history of injuries, including some that led to deaths, park officials announced Tuesday.

The ride was first closed temporarily in July following reports of back-to-back brain injuries.

"While X2 consistently passed a multitude of safety tests, we have decided to close the ride because we believe it's the right thing to do," Brian Oerding, Six Flags Magic Mountain president, said in a statement. "Ride safety is a cornerstone of our business, and when we see guest confidence affected, we take it seriously."

Months after the ride, first called X, opened in 2002, it had to be closed to repair design flaws . Then, in 2007, it was closed again to replace the trains with lighter ones and reopened the next year as X2. It has long been one of the park's main attractions, featuring seats that spin forward and backward 360 degrees. More than 16 million people have ridden X2, Magic Mountain said in its statement.

Anne Hawley, whose son died in 2022 after riding X2, was emotional Tuesday morning after learning the ride was permanently closed. Christopher Hawley was 22 when he rode X2, stumbled after getting off of it, lost consciousness and died shortly thereafter. His family sued Magic Mountain and settled the case in August.

"We have tried for four years to do the best we can to spread awareness," Hawley said. "They finally listened."

Hawley was just one of several people who have sued Magic Mountain in connection with brain injuries.

Hilda Farias was 28 when she rode X2 in 2010 and developed a brain bleed that led to her death, according to court records. Sheila Katerelos claimed in another suit that she suffered a traumatic brain injury in 2020 after riding X2. Lucy Alvarez claimed in a third suit that she sustained a traumatic brain injury in 2021 after riding X2, causing her "great physical, mental and nervous pain and suffering."

X2 had long been hailed by ride enthusiasts for its design. The seats are on the side of the track, allowing riders' feet to dangle below or above them as their seat spins forward or backward. At the beginning, riders are taken up a slope while facing backward and, at the peak, their seats spin forward as they hurtle toward the ground headfirst.

CNN reported in August that X2 has been linked to more than a dozen reports of serious injuries and hospitalizations over the last two decades, including the deaths of Hawley and Farias. The report said two people suffered brain hemorrhages in July after riding X2, requiring surgical intervention.

The ride was closed temporarily soon after those injuries, and the state agency overseeing amusement parks, the California Division of Occupational Safety and Health, launched an inspection. That inspection is ongoing, agency spokesperson Denisse Gómez said in an emailed statement.

Martin Lewison, a roller-coaster enthusiast and a professor at Farmingdale State College in New York who's known for riding thousands of coasters around the world, said that while X2's closure was "a sad day for the coaster enthusiast world," he believed that if the ride has caused injuries and opened the company to legal risk, it made sense for Magic Mountain to close it. Lewison is a Six Flags shareholder.

Concerns about injuries on roller coasters have spanned decades.

A report by The Times in 2001 noted several studies suggested specific brain injuries were linked to thrill rides, though the data, The Times noted, were inconclusive. That same year, a rider on Magic Mountain's Goliath coaster died of a brain aneurysm. The Los Angeles County coroner concluded the ride did not cause the aneurysm "but only caused a rupture of a preexisting, severe and fragile aneurysm." The rider's family later sued.

Magic Mountain is set to open the Thrill Glider next year, a roller coaster featuring a "suspended glider train design combined with over half a mile of twisting, turning, diving track built into the park's unique mountainside," Six Flags wrote in its statement announcing the coaster's construction.

"Where else than at the Thrill Capital of the World would you expect to find a next-generation, first-of-its-kind coaster?" the company wrote.

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

articles.title: Lindsay Clancy, accused of killing 3 children, returns to court after mistrial
articles.summary: Lindsay Clancy, accused of murdering her three children, appeared in court after a mistrial as her defense seeks a not guilty verdict and no retrial. The implications of her mental health and jury dynamics are at the center of the ongoing case.
articles.body: US mother Lindsay Clancy returned to court Tuesday for the first hearing since her murder trial ended in a mistrial, as her lawyers asked a Massachusetts judge to enter a finding of not guilty and sought to block any retrial.Clancy, 36, faces three first-degree murder charges over the deaths of her children, Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, eight months, at the family’s home in Duxbury, Massachusetts, in January 2023. Her first trial ended on September 4 after the 12-member jury failed to reach a unanimous verdict.Prosecutors said the evidence at trial showed that Clancy strangled the children with exercise bands in the basement of the family’s Duxbury home on January 24, 2023. They said she then cut herself with a knife and jumped from a second-storey window in an apparent suicide attempt, leaving her paralysed.Defence lawyer Kevin Reddington argued that there was a “total and complete lack of evidence” from which a rational juror could find Clancy guilty. He also argued that prosecutors had not proved beyond a reasonable doubt that she was criminally responsible at the time of the deaths.The Reddington says Clancy was experiencing postpartum psychosis and should be found not guilty by reason of insanity, described under Massachusetts law as a lack of criminal responsibility. Prosecutors opposed the request, maintaining that the evidence presented at trial was sufficient to support the charges.The jury was reported to have been split 11–1 in favour of finding Clancy not guilty by reason of insanity, but it could not reach the unanimous verdict required under Massachusetts law. The jury had considered first-degree murder, second-degree murder, manslaughter and lack of criminal responsibility during its deliberations.Prosecutors have not said whether they will seek a second trial. Judge William Sullivan made no ruling Tuesday on the defence request for a not-guilty finding or on other defence motions.Sullivan scheduled another hearing for November 2 to address outstanding motions, including a bid to dismiss the murder charges and a request for a limited inquiry into the lone holdout juror. He also told the parties to be prepared to discuss a possible retrial date.The defence has argued that the mistrial should not have been declared and that another trial would violate Clancy’s protection against double jeopardy. It has also sought access to material relating to the holdout juror, Michael Desronvil, over allegations concerning cellphone use during deliberations and information provided during jury selection. Those allegations have not been proven.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Venezuelan delivery driver shot by ICE in Texas charged with assault; faces up to 20 years in prison
articles.summary: A Venezuelan delivery driver shot by ICE in Texas is charged with assault after allegedly attempting to flee during an arrest, facing up to 20 years in prison. His legal status and the shooting circumstances raise significant concerns about immigration enforcement.
articles.body: Federal prosecutors in Texas have charged a Venezuelan delivery driver who was shot by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent last week, alleging that he tried to flee officers during an attempted arrest.Wilber Rafael Garces-Perez, 28, faces assault charges over the September 20 incident, US Attorney Justin R. Simmons for the Western District of Texas announced on Tuesday.Prosecutors allege Garces-Perez sideswiped an ICE officer with his car and later tried to strike another officer with the vehicle. If convicted, he could face up to 20 years in prison.According to the complaint, Garces-Perez initially provided his driving licence when officers stopped him. He allegedly refused repeated requests to leave the vehicle but spoke in Spanish with an officer about moving and parking the car.The conversation was described in the court documents as pleasant and not aggressive.About a minute later, Garces-Perez allegedly closed the window and drove away. Prosecutors said the vehicle's driver's-side mirror struck an officer identified as L.G. in the torso.The complaint also alleges that Garces-Perez later attempted to hit an officer with his vehicle.Garces-Perez was stopped after immigration officials sought to arrest him over a final removal order.He entered the United States in 2024 through CBP One, a programme introduced during the Biden administration that allowed migrants to schedule appointments with US authorities to seek asylum. The programme was ended by President Donald Trump after he took office.Immigration lawyer Kate Lincoln-Goldfinch said Garces-Perez was an asylum seeker and had a valid work permit. She said he missed an immigration court hearing after the notice was sent to a previous address, after which a judge issued the removal order.Garces-Perez was shot in the back during the September 20 encounter and was later taken into federal immigration custody. articles.title: Trump banned nearly $1 billion in Canadian imports. These products are affected
articles.summary: The ban applies to hundreds of millions of dollars worth of Canadian products.
articles.body:
A United States ban of hundreds of millions of dollars worth of Canadian products took effect on Tuesday, escalating a trade war between the longtime allies and pinching imports from one of the top U.S. trade partners.

The ban applies to an array of products spanning from alcohol to motorcycles to dairy goods, White House documents show.

In all, the affected products account for $967 million worth of annual imports from Canada, Jacob Jensen, director of trade policy at the right-leaning American Action Forum, said in a blog post .

Nearly $9 of every $10 worth of impacted products belongs to the category of alcoholic beverages, making them the primary target of the ban, Jensen said. The move comes after some Canadian provinces pulled U.S.-made alcohol off of liquor store shelves, crimping sales for American producers.

The list of banned alcoholic products includes beer, wine, whiskey, vodka, rum and brandy.

The policy also bars some mopeds and motorcycles, as well as some food items featuring whey, a popular protein-rich additive derived from dairy. Molasses and non-alcoholic beer also stand among the banned imports.

Still, the U.S. ban applies to a small fraction of U.S. imports from Canada. The U.S. imported roughly $381 billion worth of goods in 2025, the Office of the United States Trade Representative found, meaning the ban covers 0.2% of Canadian products shipped to the U.S.

The Toasts Not Tariffs Coalition -- a trade group representing farmers, retailers and other members of the U.S. alcohol supply chain -- issued a statement on Tuesday criticizing the ban.

"We appreciate the Trump administration's commitment to encouraging Canada to reopen its market to American spirits and wine products," the organization told ABC News.

"However, as this ban on Canadian spirits and wines takes effect today, America's restaurants, bars, retailers and consumers are being pulled further into a trade dispute that has already taken a significant toll on U.S. wine and spirits producers," the group added.

A tit-for-tat trade war erupted in August after official negotiations collapsed and a fresh round of U.S. levies took hold. Within days, Canadian officials unveiled what they described as a set of matching tariffs.

Canada's retaliatory measure , which took effect earlier this month, targets about $20 billion worth of U.S. products, mirroring the size of the U.S. levies.

The goods impacted by both countries' levies total about 4.5% of annual trade between the U.S. and Canada, the Office of the United States Trade Representative said. For now, levies apply to a sliver of goods that travel between the U.S. and Canada, limiting the impact of the trade dispute.

Trump has carried out on-again, off-again trade negotiations with Canada since he took office, aiming to resolve a dispute that began with tariffs announced by Trump early in his second term.

Trump has repeatedly claimed Canada takes advantage of its proximity to the large U.S. consumer market, while preventing many U.S. sellers from reaching Canadian shoppers.

"On Trade, and in other ways, also, they are among the worst Nations in the World to deal with," Trump said on his social media platform in August. "They feel entitled, and yet, WE DON'T NEED CANADA, THEY NEED US!"

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has criticized fresh U.S. tariffs as a pressure campaign that disadvantages Canadian exporters, describing retaliatory levies as an effort to protect Canada's economy.

"I don't believe in escalating the conflict. That's not constructive, but our tariffs are necessary to protect our workers, protect our companies and our communities. We can't let American goods into Canada tariff-free while they charge our companies to export," Carney said in a video message posted earlier this month.

articles.title: Forty-five North Carolina property owners sued over roads planned through their neighborhoods for the 1,800-home Hilton Bluffs project; the developer removed both links, then the county denied its revised one-access plan
articles.summary: A legal dispute over access roads for a planned 1,800-home development in North Carolina has led to revised site plans being rejected.
articles.body: A legal dispute over access roads for a planned 1,800-home development in North Carolina has led to revised site plans being rejected. The dispute began after 45 property owners took legal action to stop proposed roads from passing through their neighbourhoods. Development company Copper Builders faced a lawsuit filed in Superior Court on behalf of local residents. The first project plans showed access roads crossing existing private properties in New Hanover County. After residents challenged the plans, the developer removed both disputed road links and submitted a new site plan using one entrance along Sledge Road. However, local authorities rejected the single-entrance plan during technical reviews. Officials cited strict safety rules for emergency vehicle access at large residential developments. As reported by Port City Daily, the dispute has left the future of the multi-million-pound Hilton Bluffs project uncertain ahead of upcoming appeal hearings.Easement disputes spark court actionThe dispute began when nearby property owners learned that early plans for Hilton Bluffs included road connections across their land. The development site is in the Sledge Forest area near Castle Hayne, a low-lying rural part of New Hanover County. Lawyers for 45 affected homeowners filed a complaint in Superior Court. They argued that Copper Builders did not have the legal easements needed to build public roads across private properties. Court documents cited by Port City Daily named several landowners who refused to sell access rights. They included Nuclear Fuel Holding Co. Inc. and individual local residents. Attorney Ned Richardson, who represents the neighbouring property owners, argued that the developer tried to get project approval without first securing valid property agreements. The Southern Environmental Law Center also filed a formal appeal against the county's initial site approval. It alleged that the proposed road system broke local land-use rules and environmental guidelines. As legal action increased, Copper Builders began talks with neighbouring groups. The company agreed to remove the disputed access points from its engineering plans.Single entry plan rejected over safety rulesTo settle the dispute with local residents, Copper Builders submitted revised plans to the New Hanover County Technical Review Committee. The new plans removed the two disputed neighbourhood connections. This left Sledge Road as the only entrance and exit for the entire 1,800-home project. County planning and emergency officials quickly raised concerns about traffic and fire safety. Under the North Carolina Fire Code and local subdivision rules, residential developments with more than 30 homes generally need at least two separate working access roads. This allows emergency vehicles to enter if one road is blocked by a storm or accident. The local fire marshal said during early technical talks that structural measures could potentially be considered to address the issue. However, county planning officers ultimately rejected the single-access layout during the formal review. Port City Daily reported that county officials decided one access road could not safely handle the amount of traffic expected from an 1,800-home community. The decision left Copper Builders without an approved site plan that would allow ground preparation to begin on the property.Legal manoeuvres delay administrative appealsThe project faced more delays when the New Hanover County Board of Adjustment met to consider pending appeals from community groups and the Southern Environmental Law Center. During recent board proceedings, lawyers for Copper Builders used an unusual approach. They asked the review board to dismiss the current community appeals while also arguing that the original site plan approved in March was still legally valid. Attorney Sam Franck, representing the developer, said the earlier approvals remained legally binding despite the later changes to the access roads. As reported by Port City Daily, community lawyers strongly rejected the developer's arguments during the hearing. Attorney Jason Keelin, who represents regional environmental groups, told the board: "They're not going to follow the plan that has been conditionally approved; therefore, we don't need to stay. We're not worried about that." The Board of Adjustment voted to delay a final decision. It told both sides to prepare full legal arguments on the appeal for a hearing scheduled for 4 November at the New Hanover County Government Center. Board member Michael Sanclimenti urged everyone involved to prepare clear legal evidence. During the recorded proceedings, he said: "Let's try to end this thing."Regional pressure on coastal infrastructureThe dispute over Hilton Bluffs shows some of the growing challenges caused by rapid housing growth across coastal North Carolina. New Hanover County has seen major population growth over the past decade. This has increased pressure on rural roads, stormwater systems and natural habitats. Local environmental groups, including those working under the Save Sledge Forest banner, have argued that large housing projects threaten regional ecosystems and increase flood risks in low-lying coastal areas. A separate agreement announced by the North Carolina Coastal Land Trust sought to protect 3,200 acres of nearby forestland. However, local conservation groups said legal disputes over traffic safety and water quality would continue. With the site plans stalled and local permits still unresolved, construction has not started on the Sledge Road property. articles.title: Can’t deny employee security clearance based on kin’s antecedents: J&K high court
articles.summary: SRINAGAR: A Jammu and Kashmir high court (HC) panel Tuesday rejected a CID report against an HC staffer, observing that an employee cannot be denied
articles.body: SRINAGAR: A Jammu and Kashmir high court (HC) panel Tuesday rejected a CID report against an HC staffer, observing that an employee cannot be denied security clearance solely because of his brother’s alleged antecedents.HC engaged Pampore resident Firdous Ahmad Sheikh as a daily-rated worker on April 1, 2010, and posted him at its Srinagar wing. On July 4, 2024, HC regularised his services as an orderly under the Regularization of Services of Daily Wagers in the High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh Regulations, 2022.Like other appointments, Firdous’s regularisation was subject to CID verification, as is required for govt employment in J&K. On Jan 1, 2026, CID denied him security clearance, citing the “heightened adversity of his brother, Abdul Qayoom Sheikh”.The matter was placed before the Chief Justice, who referred it to the Committee for Appointment and Promotion of Officials, Officers of the High Court Staff, for consideration.The committee verified Firdous’s testimonials and found them genuine. It said CID’s denial of security clearance was not based on any adverse material concerning his conduct, integrity, character or antecedents but stemmed exclusively from “the alleged antecedents of his brother and the perceived possibility of a security risk arising therefrom”.The panel said Firdous had served the HC since 2010, and nothing adverse had been reported about his conduct, integrity or performance. “On the contrary, the record reflects that his work and conduct have remained satisfactory and that no vigilance enquiry or complaint is pending against him,” it said.Quoting J&K HC’s Feb 11, 2025 judgment in the Mohd Amir Malik v. Union of India and others case—which held that a person cannot be deprived of his legal or service rights solely on account of the conduct or antecedents of his relatives—the panel noted that liability cannot be fastened upon an individual merely on account of the alleged acts or antecedents of a close relative in the absence of any cogent material establishing the individual’s own involvement, association, complicity or misconduct.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Indiana removed 3,550 feet of dangerous mine walls and restored 71 acres in a former coal-mining forest
articles.summary: A reclamation project in Greene-Sullivan State Forest, near Pleasantville in Sullivan County, Indiana, has won the highest regional award that the federal
articles.body: A reclamation project in Greene-Sullivan State Forest, near Pleasantville in Sullivan County, Indiana, has won the highest regional award that the federal Office of Surface Mining Reclamation and Enforcement presents each year. According to the Indiana Department of Natural Resources, the South Lake Highwall Project eliminated 3,550 linear feet of dangerous highwalls and revegetated 71 of its more than 81 acres. The release lists enhanced wildlife habitat among the results. DNR's Abandoned Mine Land program carried out the work with the DNR Division of Forestry and Jefferson Township. The sections below set out what the release says about it.How did Indiana’s South Lake Highwall Project restore the forestAccording to the release, the honour is called the Interior States Region Abandoned Mine Land (AML) Reclamation Award. It was presented to DNR Reclamation's AML program at the National Association of Abandoned Mine Land Programs conference on 6 October 2025. The release describes it as the highest regional award that OSMRE presents annually. The winning project is named the South Lake Highwall Project. It combined the work of DNR's AML program with the cooperative efforts of the DNR Division of Forestry and Jefferson Township.The release includes comments from state and federal officials. OSMRE Director Lanny Erdos said the Abandoned Mine Land Reclamation Awards recognise the most outstanding examples of reclamation work in the nation, and that Indiana continues to distinguish itself through consistent excellence. He said the project shows how innovation and strong community collaboration can "turn legacy coal mining hazards into safer, more sustainable spaces." According to Governor Mike Braun, reclaiming former mine land makes Indiana's forests safer, healthier and more accessible, while restoring land for recreation, wildlife and future generations.How were 3,550 feet of highwalls eliminatedThe release states that the project covered more than 81 acres. Of these, 10.5 acres were water and 71 acres were revegetated. A total of 3,550 linear feet of dangerous highwalls were eliminated, and roughly 49 acres of spoil slopes were graded. According to the release, AML projects are designed to transform former mine land so that safety, health and environmental hazards are restored or addressed.The release also describes work on water and waste. At least five acid seeps were addressed. A number of deposits of coal waste and other materials were buried to prevent acid mine drainage. Kit Turpin, DNR's AML program director, said in the release that the work on Greene-Sullivan State Forest demonstrates how thoughtful engineering and planning can restore naturalised beauty and native hardwoods and improve water quality on a post-industrial landscape.How did the project improve recreation and accessibilityAccording to the release, the project delivered benefits beyond safety and environmental improvements. It provided improved ecological services and increased quality hardwoods. It also added hardwood regeneration research plots and increased accessibility, including opportunities for recreation. The release adds that the project enhanced wildlife habitat. These outcomes are listed for the project as a whole.Turpin said the project made major gains in recreational accessibility, so that all Hoosiers can enjoy those benefits. DNR Director Alan Morrison said that, thanks to the work and collaboration on projects like this, many now-favourite spots for outdoor recreation across southern Indiana are former coal mining sites that visitors would never know had been mined. He called the award-winning project at Greene-Sullivan State Forest an excellent example of work that reclaims former mine land for safety and recreation.How long has Indiana’s AML program been reclaiming mine landThe release says the award continues Indiana AML's award-winning tradition. The program also earned the Interior States Award in 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2022 and 2024. The Abandoned Mine Land Reclamation Awards were established in 1992. They recognise exemplary state and Tribal reclamation projects that reclaim coal mine sites abandoned before the signing of the Surface Mining Control and Reclamation Act of 1977. Since 1982, Indiana's AML program has restored more than 2,600 AML construction sites, covering approximately 25,659 acres of pre-law abandoned coal mines and related impacts.DNR administers the surface coal mining laws for Indiana. The release says the AML program is responsible for eliminating threats to the public and environment that remain from coal mining activity before the enactment of current law. It is available to public and private landowners experiencing negative impacts from legacy mining. Because reclamation funding is distributed based on need, the program is cataloguing future projects, and Indiana's eligibility for federal grants depends on the state's inventory of abandoned mine land.You use AI every day. articles.title: Ukrainian fitness influencer Vadym Oleynik, partner Olena Kravchenko face backlash after riding nesting sea turtle and handling hatchlings in Oman despite volunteers monitoring site
articles.summary: A Ukrainian fitness influencer has faced widespread criticism after images appeared to show him and his partner sitting on a nesting sea turtle and
articles.body: A Ukrainian fitness influencer has faced widespread criticism after images appeared to show him and his partner sitting on a nesting sea turtle and handling newly hatched turtles in Oman. Authorities said the incident violated wildlife protection laws.Vadym Oleynik, 32, was visiting the Ras al Hadd area of Oman with his partner, cosmetic doctor Olena Kravchenko, when the incident reportedly took place. The coastal region is known as an important nesting site for several species of sea turtles.As Jam Press reported, the couple were accompanied by volunteers from an environmental organisation that was monitoring turtle nesting activity when the alleged incidents occurred.Images circulating online appeared to show Oleynik and Kravchenko taking turns sitting on the shell of a sea turtle as it was nesting and laying eggs. Oleynik was also seen picking up newly hatched turtles.The images sparked a backlash from conservationists and social media users, particularly because the turtle was reportedly in the middle of its nesting process.Conservation group criticises incidentItalian conservation project Biologicamente was among the first organisations to draw attention to the images. The group criticised both the individuals involved and the environmental organisation whose volunteers were reportedly present at the site.It questioned how volunteers could have allowed anyone to sit on a nesting turtle merely for photographs and described the incident as exploitation and mistreatment of wildlife.The images were reportedly shared with Oleynik’s approximately 200,000 Instagram followers. Following the backlash, comments on his social media account were reportedly disabled.Oman authorities say wildlife laws were violatedOman’s Environment Authority later said Oleynik’s actions violated laws and regulations designed to protect wildlife.The authority said it had taken the “necessary legal action” against the individual involved in accordance with applicable legislation. It also stressed its opposition to behaviour that could harm wildlife or threaten natural habitats.Some reports subsequently claimed that Oleynik and Kravchenko had been detained by police. However, there has been no official confirmation of their reported detention.Oleynik has continued posting photographs and videos from his holiday following the incident.Influencer apologisesOleynik has since apologised for his actions and said he did not intend to harm the turtle.“I didn’t see the rules. I made a mistake and apologise to everyone,” he said.He also claimed that he had been misled by the organisation accompanying them and maintained that he had not intended to cause harm.Oleynik describes himself as a fitness influencer, calisthenics champion and Master of Sport in combat sambo. His social media accounts have a substantial following.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
